features.description: Capability cards surface the RESOLVING guidance command, not a status-refresh. In operator_console.provide_capability_actions, for a capability whose status requires setup (the needs_setup / blocked / not_installed branches) set exact_command to the guidance command `dontpanic capabilities setup <id> --print-steps` instead of `dontpanic capabilities status <id>` (a read-only diagnostic). The plain_consequence must honestly say it PRINTS the setup steps / guidance — never imply it auto-fixes. Keep the item non-automatable and keep the existing operator-attested resolution with the capability_ready clears_when (resolution is still on evidence: a later re-probe reporting ready), because --print-steps does not itself resolve the card.
steps: operator_console.provide_capability_actions: change exact_command for the setup-requiring branches to `dontpanic capabilities setup <id> --print-steps`
Rewrite plain_consequence to 'Prints the setup steps for <id> so you can complete it.' (guidance, not fix)
Preserve automatable=False, the operator-attested resolution class, and the capability_ready clears_when (clear on re-probe); reversible=True (printing steps is read-only)
Tests: a setup-requiring capability card carries the setup --print-steps command (not status), an honest consequence, and still clears on a later ready re-probe
features.acceptance: For capability cards requiring setup, the emitted command is `dontpanic capabilities setup <id> --print-steps`; the card stays non-automatable and clears only after a later capability re-probe reports the tool ready. The consequence text says it prints the setup steps (guidance), never that it auto-fixes. Verified by producer tests over the emitted command, the non-automatable flag, and the clear-on-ready behaviour.

features.description: Plain-language card detail. Replace the raw `detail = 'missing: <token, token, …>'` blob with a short human-legible summary built from the capability manifest's setup_steps[].what plus the human-required reasons, so a non-technical operator can read what the setup is and why a human is needed. Fall back to the existing missing-token summary only when no setup steps are available.
steps: Resolve the capability's setup steps (from the manifest / status envelope) for the card's id
Build detail from each step's plain 'what' text (and the human-required reason for human steps), summarized and short
Fallback to the prior missing-token summary when no setup steps exist
Tests: a capability with setup steps renders what/why detail (no raw token blob); one without falls back to the missing summary
features.acceptance: Capability card detail reads as plain-language step descriptions plus human-required reasons (not a raw token list), with a graceful fallback to the missing summary when no steps exist. Verified by render tests for both the with-steps and no-steps cases.

features.description: Producer/data: mark install-level capability work as a global group. The capability ActionItems (and/or the exported dashboard state) carry a scope/group label such as `global_tool_setup` that identifies these as install-level GLOBAL tools, distinct from tracked projects. This is the data seam the dashboard renders in F004 — no rendering here, just the label on the producer output.
steps: Add a stable group label (e.g. `global_tool_setup`) to capability-sourced ActionItems / exported state
Ensure the label is carried through state_projection / the served dashboard state
Tests: a producer test asserts capability items expose the global-tool group label; non-capability items do not
features.acceptance: Capability-sourced ActionItems and the exported state projection carry a group label marking them as install-level global tools, distinct from project-scoped items. Verified by a producer test asserting the label is present on capability items and absent on others.

features.description: Dashboard rendering: display 'Global tools' separately from 'Tracked projects'. The Health / What Now surface groups the F003-labelled install-level tools under a clearly-labelled 'Global tools' heading, distinct from the 'Tracked projects' count/list, with copy clarifying that global tools are install-level and need no project registration (so 'DontPanic isn't tracked' never reads as a capability problem).
steps: Dashboard health/what-now: render the F003 global-tool group under a 'Global tools' label, separate from 'Tracked projects'
Add copy clarifying global tools are install-level and not per-project
Tests: a dashboard render test asserts both the 'Global tools' and 'Tracked projects' labels render distinctly
features.acceptance: The dashboard groups the install-level tools under a 'Global tools' heading, separate from the tracked-projects list, with copy clarifying global tools are install-level. Verified by a dashboard render test asserting both headings render distinctly.

features.description: Fleet surface shows Global tools (correctness). build_fleet_what_now only aggregates the TRACKED projects' caches; install-level capability items live in the DontPanic repo (not a tracked project), so they never enter the fleet envelope (0 capability items in fleet-what-now.json) and the All-Projects/fleet view cannot render 'Global tools'. (1) Include the install-level capability items in fleet-what-now.json via a reusable dashboard.gather_install_capability_items() seam (run_status -> _scope_envelope_to_v0_local -> provide_capability_actions). (2) Preserve the group=global_tool_setup tag through the fleet render boundary (the payload uses to_dict() which bypasses action_view, so derive group inline mirroring F003). (3) DEDUP GUARD: render global-tool items ONLY in the dedicated 'Global tools' block (renderGlobalToolsHTML) and FILTER them out of project grouping (groupByProject must not also place them in the __global__ section). Re-derive global-tool identity in JS (group===global_tool_setup OR source===capability) so it is robust even if a producer omits the tag.
steps: dashboard.gather_install_capability_items(repo_root=None) -> tuple[ActionItem] (best-effort, empty on failure)
build_fleet_what_now: append install capability items to all_items; derive group=global_tool_setup on capability-source items in the to_dict payload
what-now-logic: isGlobalToolItem(item) = group===GLOBAL_TOOL_GROUP || source==='capability'; renderGlobalToolsHTML filters by it
what-now-logic: groupByProject excludes isGlobalToolItem items (dedup guard) so they never render in the __global__ project section
Tests: fleet build includes >=1 capability item carrying group; groupByProject drops global-tool items while keeping reconcile globals; renderGlobalToolsHTML renders them once
features.acceptance: fleet-what-now.json includes the install-level capability items carrying group=global_tool_setup, and the All-Projects/fleet view renders them once under a dedicated 'Global tools' block with NO duplicate in the project/__global__ grouping. Verified by a Python test (fleet build carries capability items + group) and JS tests (groupByProject excludes global-tool items; renderGlobalToolsHTML renders them; reconcile globals are untouched).

features.description: Health-tab affordance (secondary). The Health 'Setup incomplete' install-readiness card is where a human naturally interprets install state, so label it explicitly as Global tools. renderInstallHealthCardHTML gets a 'Global tools' label + clarifying copy (install-level, not tied to a project), distinct from the page's 'N projects tracked' header.
steps: health-logic.renderInstallHealthCardHTML: add a 'Global tools' label/heading + 'install-level, not tied to a project' clarifying copy
Keep the existing GLOBAL scope badge + source line
Tests: renderInstallHealthCardHTML output contains 'Global tools' + the clarifying copy
features.acceptance: The Health install-readiness card explicitly labels install state as 'Global tools' with install-level clarifying copy, distinct from the tracked-projects header. Verified by a health-logic render test.
